name: Main Page Text Block
description:
A sauna fan is easy to ignore until it stops. When the cabin fan or the blower behind the heater bay fails, warm air stops circulating: the cabin heats unevenly, moisture lingers long after a session, and the electronics in the power box run hotter than they were designed to.

Almost every infrared cabin uses a small 110-120V axial fan behind a vent grille, a blower in the heater bay, or a cooling fan inside the control box - and all three are replaceable without touching the rest of the cabin. We stock circulation, exhaust and control-box fans for infrared saunas of most brands, including discontinued cabins whose original part number is long out of production.

Send a photo of the old fan and of the label inside your cabin, and a specialist confirms the fitment before you order.
